name: Notion
one_liner: Notion API allows reading, creating, and updating pages, databases, users, comments, and more via REST.
auth_notes: Requests use the HTTP `Authorization` header to both authenticate and authorize operations. The Notion API accepts bearer tokens in this header.
access_notes: You can create your own, internal connections, public connections, and personal access tokens — all powered by the same REST API.

extras.rate_limits: The Notion API enforces two rate limits: Per connection — an average of three requests per second, with some bursts beyond the average allowed.

evidence.snippet: Requests use the HTTP `Authorization` header to both authenticate and authorize operations. The Notion API accepts bearer tokens in this header.
With the REST API, you can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace — pages, databases, users, comments, and more.
The fastest way to start building is the Quickstart — create a personal access token, make your first API request, and see a new page appear in your workspace in under two minutes.
Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

If you need headless or fully automated access, you can use the [open-source MCP server](https://github.com/makenotion/notion-mcp-server) with a Notion API token, though this package is no longer actively maintained.
